prompt.en: A station has separate unbonded ground rods for the tower and operating desk. What is the safety concern?

text.en: The rods can develop dangerous voltage differences during a fault or surge
The transmitter will automatically change frequency
The antenna polarization will become circular
The receiver squelch will stop muting noise

explanation.en: Bonding electrodes together reduces voltage differences that could otherwise put surge or fault current through station equipment.

prompt.en: A desk radio's only lightning protector is mounted behind the transceiver after the cable has crossed the room. What improvement best matches the lesson?

text.en: Move the protector to the antenna feed point at the top of the mast
Install the protector at the outside entry point and bond it there
Use a longer indoor coax loop before the radio

explanation.en: Surge energy should be diverted at the entry and grounding point before it is routed through the operating position.

prompt.en: You plan to use an indoor transmitting antenna during a short low-power test. Which setup gives the best RF-safety margin?

text.en: Place it beside the operating chair to shorten the coax
Aim a high-gain beam through an occupied room
Hang it where people can brush against the feed point
Keep it as far as practical from occupied spaces and control access

explanation.en: Distance and access control are conservative RF-safety tools, especially for indoor antennas.
